_about: Read by tools, not by the model: tools/lint_deck.py loads this file. The runtime
card is references/cards/lint.md.
Measured with python-pptx from the reference Workforce Optimization deck — the
exemplar the builder fills, assets/exemplar/wfo-sales-deck.pptx (10 slides,
13.333 x 7.5 in). `reference_slides` is what that file actually contains, slide
by slide; `deck_slides` is what lint_deck.py holds a BUILT deck to, keyed by this
anatomy's slide numbers, each carrying the exemplar slide it was measured from.
Re-measure and rewrite this file if the exemplar changes; never append to it.
The faces the reference actually uses. Its runs name only 'Replica LL TT'; the
titles and the theme-referenced runs (+mj-lt, +mn-lt, +mn-ea, +mn-cs) resolve
through the deck's own theme to Azurio and Replica LL TT. The two symbol faces
are the ones PowerPoint itself attaches to the glyph runs in the package tables
(the filled and half-filled circles); nothing else is a brand face.
lint_deck.py compares case-insensitively and ignores spaces, hyphens and a
trailing weight, so 'ReplicaLLTT-Regular' and 'Replica LL TT' are one face.
prstGeom roundRect adjustment values in the reference. Everything structural —
cards, panels, the platform container, diagram boxes — sits at 4000-12000, which
is 0.04-0.18 in on a shape inches wide: it reads square at slide scale. Only
chips and vendor badges are real pills, at 50000, and they are all small.
So lint_deck.py counts a shape as rounded only above `pill_adj_min`, and calls
anything rounded and taller than `pill_max_h_in` a rounded card, which the
reference has none of.

2.note: six roundRect, of which three are pills (the KPI chips); the two cards and the anchor strip sit at 4000-12000

4.note: the three pictures are the before image, the after image and the customer's logo

5.note: the three stat tiles are roundRect at 10000 — square at slide scale, not pills; the picture is the customer's logo

6.note: ten roundRect, of which two are pills (the NVIDIA and Oracle vendor badges)

7.note: every roundRect here sits at 5000 — the container, the app, the engine and the source boxes all read square

cover._about: Reference slide 1, on the Title-AI photo layout: the dark ground and the hero photo come from the layout, the slide carries three shapes. `layout` and `layout_pictures` are what lint_deck.py holds a built cover to — the cover must sit on this layout and a picture must reach it, from the layout or from the slide; an ink-only cover is an unfinished state.
cover.layout_pictures_note: on the layout: `Picture 4` (the hero) and `Logo` (the mark); `Image 2` is a freeform mask, not a picture
cover.dropped: The tier line the reference carried on the lower block ('PROOF OF VALUE · ROLL-OUT · SCALING') — the owner asked for no tier line on the cover; the builder reuses that shape for the ICP line.

vertical_icons._about: Reference slide 3: one picture per card, centred in the card's blue panel.

image_slots._about: Reference slide 4: the two before/after pictures.

_about: Reference slide 5 — the delivered case, in the composition lint_deck.py holds every
built proof slide to: the customer's logo top-left, a headline stating the delivered
outcome, three stat tiles, four labelled quadrants, the anchor strip, the caveat
footnote. `quadrants` is the reference's own four labels with the top-left corner of
each label textbox, in reading order (top row left to right, then the bottom row);
`stat_tiles` is the top-left corner of each tile's value and label textbox. A shape is
taken to be that slot when its top-left corner is within `match_tol_in` of the recorded
one — the builder fills these shapes and never moves them.
The logo is placed only when the pack brief clears the customer's name for the channel
being linted AND `deck.images.customer_logo` names a file; otherwise the slide carries
no picture at all.

architecture._about: Reference slide 7. Two columns: the source boxes on the left, the platform container on the right. The builder adds a third column, at the source boxes' own geometry, only when the spec names a system that receives the result but is not also a source.

table_type._about: Reference slides 8-10. The floors in `deck_slides` are these numbers.

_about: What lint_deck.py holds a built deck to, per anatomy slide. `exemplar_slide` is
where each number was measured; `ref_rounded` / `ref_pictures` are the
exemplar's own counts on that slide. `max_rounded` is `ref_rounded` plus the
pills the anatomy legitimately repeats per spec item (chips, numeral badges,
vendor badges) — a pill is small by construction, and any rounded shape taller
than corner_radius.pill_max_h_in fails as a rounded card whatever the count.
`max_pictures` is the exemplar's own count, except the cover, where the anatomy
has a photo slot the exemplar keeps on its layout.

1.note: the hero photo lives on the Title-AI layout; a builder that places it on the slide gets one picture

2.note: the three KPI chips; the two cards and the anchor strip are square

3.note: one icon per industry card, and the cards are square

5.note: the reference's stat tiles are square; the allowance is the numbered step badges the anatomy adds, up to six

6.note: no peer in the reference — it was the seller quadrant of slide 5; the allowance is one numeral badge per quadrant

7.note: one vendor badge per ladder row; the ladder panels themselves are square

8.note: every box on the reference's diagram reads square
